subject: Private control plane access: SAML / SCIM mapping + deployment checklist
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finserv.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Private control plane - IdP/SCIM requirements and questions

Laura — thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and identity team reviewed the private control plane (VPC) architecture and we have a few concrete asks before legal/procurement will sign off: 

1) We need SAML SSO into the private control plane admin UI. Can Redwood act as a SAML SP and accept assertions from our IdP (Okta)? Any supported encryption/signature algorithms we should be aware of?

2) SCIM provisioning for user and group sync is required. We need an example SCIM schema and sample group-to-role mapping so our IAM team can validate.

3) Role model: we need the ability to map Okta groups to discrete "control plane roles" (admin, infra-operator, audit-reader). Can the mapping be managed via UI and/or via API?

4) Audit / traceability: timestamped admin actions, ID of authenticated principal, and evidence for when a role was changed.

5) Key rotation and IdP metadata refresh cadence (we rotate certificates every 90 days) — how is downtime avoided?

Attached: scim_schema.csv with our current canonical groups and an internal doc describing the compliance controls we must satisfy.

Can you propose a short mutual action plan and any gaps we should expect in a typical deployment?

Thanks —
Anita Shah
Director, Security Operations
FinServ Capital
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finserv.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private control plane - IdP/SCIM requirements and questions

Anita — really helpful list, thank you. High level answers inline and then a proposed MAP (mutual action plan) below. Attaching a small snippet showing our recommended IdP attributes and a short checklist you can hand to your SREs (idp-config-snippets.txt).

1) SAML SSO: Yes — Redwood private control plane acts as a SAML SP. We support HTTP-POST bindings and signed assertions. We recommend RSA-SHA256 signatures; we also support SHA1 for legacy IdPs but will flag it in the deployment notes. If you enforce encrypted assertions we'll need the IdP to provide encryption certs.

2) SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 for Users + Groups. The attached scim_schema.csv you sent maps cleanly to our SCIM schema with a couple of optional attributes (externalId and enterprise:department) — Marcus included a suggested mapping in his note.

3) Role mapping: You can manage group->role mapping both via the private control plane UI (recommended for small changes) and via our Admin API (recommended for infra-as-code deployments). Changes are audited (see 4).

4) Audit: Every admin action that affects roles, deployments, or routing is emitted to the audit log with principal, timestamp, and a change diff. We retain audit logs for configurable retention; for enterprise customers we can surface these to your SIEM via secure syslog/collector.

5) Key rotation/metadata: We support rolling certificate updates — you can upload the new IdP metadata with an overlap window so both certs are accepted for a configurable period (default 7 days). We also provide a health-check endpoint that your IdP can call post-rotation.

Proposed MAP (high level):
- Day 0: Exchange metadata & test SP-initiated SAML with a sandbox admin account (Laura + Marcus lead).
- Day 2: Enable SCIM in test org, validate group provisioning sync (Stephanie lead).
- Day 4: Configure role mappings, run an access audit report and confirm with your IAM team.
- Day 7: Run certificate rotation exercise with overlap window, verify no interruption.

Next steps: Marcus, can you attach the deploy checklist and the concrete mapping table? If Anita's team is comfortable I'll schedule a one-hour tech runbook session (we typically include your IdP engineer + our infra eng).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0199
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private control plane - IdP/SCIM requirements and questions

Laura / Steph — attaching the implementation checklist and a compact mapping matrix (redwood-deploy-checklist.pdf). Summary here so Anita can see specifics quickly: 

- SCIM attributes: map externalId -> id, email -> userName, groups[].value -> group.displayName. We include enterprise:roles as optional attribute for downstream systems.
- Role mapping example:
  * Okta group "FinServ_Admins" => control-plane role "admin" (full deploy + billing visibility)
  * Okta group "FinServ_Infra" => control-plane role "infra-operator" (deploy, scale, instance logs)
  * Okta group "FinServ_Audit" => control-plane role "audit-reader" (read-only audit logs)
- Recommended API flow for IaC: POST /admin/v1/role-mappings with a JSON payload we generate — we'll share a sample curl in the runbook.
- Edge cases: SCIM deprovision -> we recommend soft-deactivate in control plane for 24h before hard-delete to avoid accidental data+config loss.

I'll prepare the sample curl and add it to the runbook before the tech session.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private control plane - IdP/SCIM requirements and questions

Hi Anita / Laura — this is Okta support. Thanks for the details. A couple of quick notes that often save time during private deployments: 

- Ensure the SP assertion consumer URL is reachable from your IdP sandbox (if you have a VPC proxy make sure the metadata points to the public metadata endpoint we agreed on).
- For encrypted assertions, provide both the certificate and the corresponding KeyID so SPs can rotate without downtime.
- SCIM rate limits: set provisioning window to 1–5 minutes for group-heavy orgs; if FinServ has >10k users we recommend bulk sync during the maintenance window.
- We attached an Okta SAML checklist link: https://help.okta.com/saml-config (also in your thread metadata).

If you'd like, we can join the tech session and walk the IdP engineer through the metadata exchange live.

Regards,
Okta Support Team
